findings.reason: the plan must specify extending `_AuthoredProseParser` to return prose keyed by section identity (or name the mechanism that does so), or the `_section_digests` map cannot be built.
findings.text: §16 asserts the authored-prose args (`_AuthoredProseParser`) "already keep a section stack as it streams and passes the top of that stack as the enclosing element at every heading", but `__init__` (`:178`) keeps only a list of protection booleans and the parser never computes or passes a section identity; to make the unit of review the authored section, `_section_digests` needs per-section prose, i.e. the parser must bucket its chunks by identity and separate the document-unit prose, and that change to the parser's output shape (string → identity-keyed mapping) is neither named nor assigned to an owner. Without it there is no join between the prose walk and identity, which is the interface §16 claims to expose.

findings.reason: the section must either name the two additions as distinct symbols and cite them, or state plainly that the identity function is retired into §17's reader and the family grows by two, so the count is checkable from the text alone.
findings.text: §16's interface accounting counts one public addition (the section-identity function on `reckon/_plan_html.py`) and §17 counts one for the yield reader on the same module, yet §16 (line 167) says the identity function is "the one §17 moves into the span parser", so the two additions may be a single symbol under two names; the family total is therefore stated as +3 but reads as +2.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §16's new `_section_digests(plan)` is stated to hide the whole section-unit recomposition behind a pure function that consumes "the prose parser that already keeps a section stack as it streams and passes the top of that stack as the enclosing element at every heading", but the current parser (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:178-235`) keeps no identity stack and passes no enclosing element, so the interface does not hide the behaviour it is claimed to.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the design removes duplicates and names the owner to extend at each: §17 moves the nine card/extent recognisers out of `reckon/_store.py` onto the span parser, §18 hoists `promotion._plan-remaining-sections` (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:7236`) to `reckon/_store.py` and gives the `c-run-` prefix one owner; `doccheck._implementable_section_ids` (`reckon/doccheck.py:1014`) is deliberately not folded, and §18 states the two questions and why folding would change the document check's findings.
rubric_items.interface_budget: public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23 — a finding — §16 and §17 each claim "+1 public definition on `reckon/_plan_html.py`", and §16 says its addition is "the one §17 moves into the span parser", so a reader cannot tell whether the family grows by three (§16, §17, §18) as stated or by two, because §16's identity function and §17's yield reader may be one symbol under two names. The sections name their retirements, but this ambiguity leaves the budget's own count unverifiable from the text alone.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase and cites the mechanisms it extends rather than rebuilding them: `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:44,94`), the store's `_section_heading`/`_wrapper_section_heading`/`_section_body_end`/`_landed_card_span` (`reckon/_store.py:860,899,932,992`), the AST census (`reckon/interface_counts.py:74` `definitions`, `:441` `read_trees`), and `promotion._plan_remaining_sections`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan deliberately avoids parallel wrappers: §17 "consolidates onto the parser rather than adding a scanner", §16 states why the coverage predicate "is not a wrapper over the review reader", and the new two-mapping identity function is justified by the wrapper-id case (`_store.py:860`) that a heading-only function cannot see.
